questions.questionTextEn: If the solubility product of $\text{AgCl}$ in water is $K_{sp} = 1.8 \times 10^{-10}$, its molar solubility in $0.10\text{ M}$ aqueous $\text{NaCl}$ solution is closest to
questions.explanationEn: In $0.10\text{ M NaCl}$, $[\text{Cl}^-] = 0.10 + s \approx 0.10\text{ M}$. Thus $K_{sp} = s(0.10) \implies s = \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-10}}{0.10} = 1.8 \times 10^{-9}\text{ M}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For an aqueous solution of a salt derived from a weak acid ($\text{p}K_a$) and a weak base ($\text{p}K_b$) at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$, the $\text{pH}$ is given by
questions.explanationEn: For a salt of a weak acid and a weak base (when hydrolysis is small), $\text{pH} = \frac{1}{2}(\text{p}K_w + \text{p}K_a - \text{p}K_b) = 7 + \frac{1}{2}(\text{p}K_a - \text{p}K_b)$, independent of salt concentration $C$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a van der Waals gas, the maximum Joule–Thomson inversion temperature ($T_i$) is related to its Boyle temperature ($T_B$) by
questions.explanationEn: For a van der Waals gas, $T_B = \frac{a}{Rb}$ and the maximum Joule–Thomson inversion temperature is $T_i = \frac{2a}{Rb} = 2T_B$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Benzoic acid undergoes complete dimerization ($2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} \to (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH})_2$) in benzene. The ideal van 't Hoff factor ($i$) for this solution is
questions.explanationEn: When $100\%$ of monomer molecules associate into dimers ($n = 2$), the number of solute particles is halved, so $i = 1 - \alpha\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right) = 1 - 1\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = 0.5$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Upon increasing temperature, the dynamic viscosity ($\eta$) of an ideal gas and that of a typical liquid, respectively,
questions.explanationEn: In a gas, momentum transfer increases with molecular speed ($\eta_{\text{gas}} \propto \sqrt{T}$), so gas viscosity **increases** with temperature. In a liquid, higher temperature overcomes intermolecular cohesive barriers ($\eta_{\text{liq}} = A e^{E_a/RT}$), so liquid viscosity **decreases** with temperature.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a spinel oxide crystal, oxide ions ($\text{O}^{2-}$) form a cubic close-packed (ccp) lattice, $\text{A}^{2+}$ ions occupy one-eighth of the tetrahedral voids, and $\text{B}^{3+}$ ions occupy one-half of the octahedral voids. The chemical formula of the oxide is
questions.explanationEn: Per ccp unit cell of $4$ $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions, there are $4$ octahedral voids and $8$ tetrahedral voids. Thus $\text{A}^{2+} = \frac{1}{8}(8) = 1$ and $\text{B}^{3+} = \frac{1}{2}(4) = 2$, giving the formula $\text{AB}_2\text{O}_4$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following correctly expresses the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation?
questions.explanationEn: Differentiating $G/T$ at constant $P$: $\left[\frac{\partial(G/T)}{\partial T}\right]_P = \frac{1}{T}\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P - \frac{G}{T^2} = \frac{-S}{T} - \frac{H - TS}{T^2} = -\frac{H}{T^2}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: If the molar solubility of sparingly soluble calcium phosphate, $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$, in pure water is $s\text{ mol L}^{-1}$, its solubility product $K_{sp}$ is expressed as
questions.explanationEn: Dissolution gives $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2(s) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{Ca}^{2+}(aq) + 2\text{PO}_4^{3-}(aq)$, so $[\text{Ca}^{2+}] = 3s$ and $[\text{PO}_4^{3-}] = 2s$. Thus $K_{sp} = (3s)^3(2s)^2 = 27s^3 \cdot 4s^2 = 108s^5$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Pure liquids $A$ and $B$ have vapor pressures $P_A^\circ = 60\text{ kPa}$ and $P_B^\circ = 20\text{ kPa}$, respectively, at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$. For an equimolar ideal liquid mixture of $A$ and $B$, the mole fraction of $A$ in the equilibrium vapor phase ($y_A$) is
questions.explanationEn: By Raoult's law, $P_A = x_A P_A^\circ = 0.5(60) = 30\text{ kPa}$ and $P_B = 0.5(20) = 10\text{ kPa}$, so $P_{\text{total}} = 40\text{ kPa}$. By Dalton's law, $y_A = \frac{P_A}{P_{\text{total}}} = \frac{30}{40} = 0.75$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Near absolute zero, the molar heat capacity of a non-metallic crystalline solid obeys the Debye $T^3$ law, $C_{P,m}(T) = a T^3$. Assuming $S_m(0) = 0$ by the Third Law, the molar entropy $S_m(T)$ in this temperature regime equals
questions.explanationEn: Integrating from $0$ to $T$: $S_m(T) = \int_0^T \frac{C_{P,m}(T')}{T'}\,dT' = \int_0^T a(T')^2\,dT' = \frac{1}{3}aT^3 = \frac{1}{3}C_{P,m}(T)$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn:
Which of the following aqueous mixture(s) form(s) an **acidic buffer** ($\text{pH} < 7$ at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$)?
[Given: $\text{p}K_a(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = 4.76$, $\text{p}K_a(\text{HCOOH}) = 3.75$, $\text{p}K_b(\text{NH}_3) = 4.75$]
optionsEn: $100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + 50\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$
$100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{HCOOH} + 100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{HCOONa}$
$100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + 100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$
$100\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa} + 50\text{ mL}$ of $0.1\text{ M}$ $\text{HCl}$
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** Partial neutralization leaves $5\text{ mmol}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and $5\text{ mmol}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$ ($\text{pH} = 4.76$).
- **(B) True:** Equimolar formic acid / sodium formate buffer ($\text{pH} = 3.75$).
- **(C) False:** Forms a **basic** buffer ($\text{pH} = 14 - 4.75 = 9.25$).
- **(D) True:** $\text{HCl}$ protonates half of $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$ to form $5\text{ mmol}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ and $5\text{ mmol}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$ ($\text{pH} = 4.76$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is/are valid Maxwell thermodynamic relation(s)?
questions.explanationEn: From $dU = T\,dS - P\,dV$, $dH = T\,dS + V\,dP$, $dA = -S\,dT - P\,dV$, and $dG = -S\,dT + V\,dP$: **(A)**, **(B)**, and **(C)** are exact Maxwell relations, whereas **(D)** is missing a minus sign ($(\partial S/\partial P)_T = -(\partial V/\partial T)_P$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a real gas described by the van der Waals equation $\left(P + \dfrac{an^2}{V^2}\right)(V - nb) = nRT$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The parameter $a$ has SI units of $\text{Pa m}^6\text{ mol}^{-2}$.
The parameter $b$ represents four times the actual hard-sphere molar volume of the gas molecules.
In the high-pressure limit ($P \to \infty$), the compressibility factor $Z$ approaches $0$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** $an^2/V^2$ has units of pressure ($\text{Pa}$), so $a$ has units $\text{Pa m}^6\text{ mol}^{-2}$.
- **(B) True:** $b = 4 N_A \left(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right)$.
- **(C) True:** Standard van der Waals critical constants.
- **(D) False:** At very high pressures, $Z \approx 1 + \frac{bP}{RT} > 1$ and increases linearly with $P$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding the law of corresponding states and reduced variables ($P_r = P/P_c$, $V_r = V_m/V_{m,c}$, $T_r = T/T_c$) is/are correct?
optionsEn: The reduced van der Waals equation $\left(P_r + \dfrac{3}{V_r^2}\right)(3V_r - 1) = 8T_r$ contains no gas-specific constants $a$ or $b$.
Two different van der Waals gases at the same reduced temperature $T_r$ and reduced pressure $P_r$ have the same compressibility factor $Z$.
A gas at $T_r > 1$ can always be liquefied simply by applying sufficiently high pressure.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A), (B), (C) True:** Core results of the law of corresponding states.
- **(D) False:** Above the critical temperature ($T_r > 1$, i.e., $T > T_c$), a gas cannot be liquefied by pressure alone (it forms a supercritical fluid).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of distinct Bravais lattices in three-dimensional crystallography is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: The 7 crystal systems combine with the 4 centering types (P, I, F, C) to yield exactly $14$ unique 3D Bravais lattices.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: According to the Gibbs phase rule, the number of degrees of freedom for a two-component liquid–vapor equilibrium ($C = 2, P = 2$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Using $F = C - P + 2$ with $C = 2$ and $P = 2$, we obtain $F = 2 - 2 + 2 = 2$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An ideal gas expands from $2.0\text{ L}$ to $7.0\text{ L}$ against a constant external pressure of $2.0\text{ bar}$ ($1\text{ bar} = 10^5\text{ Pa}$). The work done *on* the gas ($w$) is _______ $\text{kJ}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: At constant external pressure, $w = -P_{\text{ext}}\Delta V = -(2.0 \times 10^5\text{ Pa})(5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3) = -1000\text{ J} = -1.00\text{ kJ}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For a cubic crystal with lattice parameter $a = 6.00\text{ \AA}$, the interplanar spacing $d_{221}$ is _______ $\text{\AA}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For a cubic lattice, $d_{hkl} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{h^2 + k^2 + l^2}} = \frac{6.00}{\sqrt{2^2 + 2^2 + 1^2}} = \frac{6.00}{\sqrt{9}} = 2.00\text{ \AA}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A metal with atomic radius $r = 1.732\text{ \AA}$ crystallizes in a body-centered cubic (bcc) lattice. The unit cell edge length $a$ is _______ $\text{\AA}$. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: For a bcc lattice, $\sqrt{3}\,a = 4r \implies a = \frac{4 \times 1.732}{1.73205} = 4.00\text{ \AA}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Physical Chemistry II: States of Matter, Thermodynamics & Equilibria (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For the dissociation $\text{PCl}_5(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3(g) + \text{Cl}_2(g)$, $K_p = 1.80\text{ bar}$ at $500\text{ K}$. Starting with pure $\text{PCl}_5(g)$, its equilibrium degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) at a total pressure of $2.00\text{ bar}$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: With $K_p = \frac{\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha^2}P$, we have $\frac{\alpha^2}{1 - \alpha^2} = \frac{1.80}{2.00} = 0.90 \implies \alpha^2 = \frac{0.90}{1.90} = 0.4737 \implies \alpha = 0.688 \approx 0.69$.
